subsystems.name: Squeezing source
subsystems.role: generates squeezed vacuum by parametric down-conversion.
parts: nonlinear crystal (periodically poled potassium titanyl phosphate)
optical parametric oscillator cavity with low-loss mirrors

subsystems.name: Pump laser system
subsystems.role: supplies the coherent pump beam that drives the nonlinear process.

subsystems.name: Injection and mode-matching optics
subsystems.role: delivers the squeezed vacuum into the interferometer's dark port with minimal loss.

subsystems.name: Filter cavity
subsystems.role: rotates the squeezing angle across frequency to reduce noise in both shot-noise and radiation-pressure-limited bands.
parts: long low-loss optical cavity (hundreds of metres)

subsystems.name: Control and readout electronics
subsystems.role: locks phases, monitors squeezing level and prevents degradation of the interferometer's sensitivity.
parts: homodyne detector for offline squeezing measurement

buildSteps.title: Generate the pump beam
buildSteps.detail: A stable infrared laser is frequency-doubled to green light, filtered and actively stabilized in power and phase.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the nonlinear crystal
buildSteps.detail: A periodically poled crystal is grown, cut and coated to achieve quasi-phase-matching at the pump and squeezed-light wavelengths.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the optical parametric oscillator
buildSteps.detail: The crystal is placed in a low-loss cavity formed by highly reflective mirrors; the cavity length and temperature are tuned to resonance.

buildSteps.title: Characterize the squeezed vacuum
buildSteps.detail: The output is measured with a homodyne detector to verify the noise reduction (typically several decibels) and its frequency dependence.

buildSteps.title: Mode-match into the interferometer
buildSteps.detail: Lenses and mirrors shape the squeezed beam to match the interferometer's dark-port mode, with losses kept to a minimum.

buildSteps.title: Install and lock a filter cavity (optional)
buildSteps.detail: For frequency-dependent squeezing, a long low-loss cavity is built, aligned and locked so its reflection imparts a frequency-dependent rotation.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with detector control
buildSteps.detail: The squeezing injection is phased in while the interferometer remains locked, and the sensitivity improvement is verified across the detection band.

buildSteps.title: Operate and maintain
buildSteps.detail: Continuous monitoring keeps the squeezing level stable; optical components and vacuum are serviced during maintenance periods.

prerequisites.tech: Low-loss optical components and high-vacuum systems
prerequisites.why: any optical loss, including absorption or scattering, converts squeezed vacuum back toward ordinary vacuum and erases the benefit.

prerequisites.tech: Stable high-power lasers and second-harmonic generation
prerequisites.why: the parametric process needs a quiet, intense pump at exactly twice the squeezed-light frequency.
periodically poled crystals provide the high nonlinearity needed to produce measurable squeezing.
the squeezed vacuum is injected into an unused output port and must not disturb the main interferometer control.
demonstrated and being commissioned in advanced detectors, but not yet standard across all observatories.

pathway.milestone: squeezed-light injection in operating gravitational-wave detectors (LIGO, Virgo, GEO600, KAGRA)
pathway.unlocks: improved shot-noise-limited sensitivity and a larger observable volume of the universe.

pathway.milestone: frequency-dependent squeezing deployed in all advanced detectors
pathway.unlocks: simultaneous reduction of shot noise and radiation-pressure noise across the full detection band.

pathway.milestone: higher squeezing levels (above 10 dB) with lower optical loss
pathway.unlocks: further reach for existing detectors and more stringent tests of general relativity.

pathway.milestone: squeezed light in other precision instruments such as atomic clocks, magnetometers and future detectors
